sources.entry: MiddleDrag - Three-finger trackpad gestures for middle-click and middle-drag on macOS. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/NullPointerDepressiveDisorder/MiddleDrag) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]
MiddleDrag - Three-finger trackpad gestures for middle-click and middle-drag.

summary.one_liner: MiddleDrag is a macOS menu bar app that maps three-finger trackpad taps and drags to middle-mouse click and middle-drag.
summary.what_it_does: MiddleDrag runs in the macOS menu bar and recognizes three-finger taps as middle-clicks and three-finger drags as middle-drags, for panning or orbiting in apps that expect a middle mouse button. It reads raw touch data through Apple's private MultitouchSupport framework, so Mission Control and other system gestures are said to keep working. Settings include enable/disable, drag sensitivity (0.5x to 2x), an option to require exactly three fingers, and launch at login. The README also mentions sensitivity and smoothing configuration. Installation is offered via Homebrew cask, MacPorts, or a .pkg download from Releases, and the README describes GitHub artifact attestation for verifying downloads.
use_cases: orbit and pan in 3D CAD apps like Blender or FreeCAD
open links in background browser tabs
pan canvas in Figma or Photoshop with a trackpad
close editor tabs with a middle click
add middle mouse button to a MacBook trackpad
how_to_run: Download the latest .pkg from the Releases page and run the installer
Build from source: git clone the repo, cd MiddleDrag, ./build.sh
notable: Three-finger tap and drag mapped to middle mouse, coexisting with Mission Control and macOS gestures
Native menu bar settings UI, no terminal configuration needed
Built on a private Apple framework, which can break across macOS releases
Positions itself against BetterTouchTool, Middle, and MiddleClick in its README
Release downloads described as attested via GitHub Artifact Attestations
caveats: Requires macOS 15.0 (Sequoia) or later; macOS 26 beta listed as compatible
Needs Accessibility permissions, and must be re-granted after app updates per the troubleshooting section
Pressing hard on the trackpad may still trigger Mission Control
